content:
Ads will arrive in Apple Maps in the US and Canada later this summer. Ahead of the feature's official rollout, Apple has shared more details about what its Apple Maps ads will and won't allow.

Apple Maps ads are on the way, and Apple has also revealed the categories that will be banned.

Apple first announced plans to introduce ads in Apple Maps back in March. The company said ads would appear at the top of search results, as well as in a new "Suggested Places" widget within the app.

Apple laid the groundwork for this in May with iOS 26.5, which included the new "Suggested Places" feature. However, the company hasn't updated the actual launch timeline for Apple Maps ads since then.

As spotted by TechCrunch, Apple has now updated its Apple Advertising Services guidelines with new information related to Apple Maps.

The guidelines cover ads across Apple News, Stocks, and Maps, and include a list of prohibited content that applies to ads on all services, such as violence, weapons, drugs, and more.

Perhaps the most notable detail is the additional, specific restrictions for Apple Maps ads. Apple says there are three more categories of content banned for Apple Maps ads:

  • Home services: Ad content that includes or directly or indirectly promotes home services, including but not limited to services such as plumbing, locksmiths, HVAC systems, pest control, roofing, or general contracting.
  • Bail bonds: Ad content that includes or directly or indirectly promotes bail bonds or bond services related to pretrial release in criminal cases.
  • Crypto ATMs: Ad content that includes or directly or indirectly promotes cryptocurrency ATMs.

Additionally, Apple says ads related to healthcare services will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis.

As TechCrunch points out, Apple's decision to ban the entire "home services" category from advertising is rather curious. While this is one of the major ad categories for Google Maps, Apple clearly has no interest in bringing these types of ads to Apple Maps.

All signs point to Apple being on the verge of launching ads in Apple Maps. However, the company still hasn't announced an official launch date.

For the complete list of all banned ad categories across Apple's services, you can visit the company's website.
